theory.intro: Use $60$ seconds per minute, $60$ minutes per hour and $24$ hours per day. Convert each link in turn; mixed units and clock formats need different handling.
facts: $1\text{ minute} = 60\text{ seconds}$, $1\text{ hour} = 60\text{ minutes} = 3600\text{ seconds}$, and $1\text{ day} = 24\text{ hours}$.
To convert to a smaller unit of time, **multiply** by $60$ or $24$.
To convert to a larger unit of time, **divide** by $60$ or $24$.
To write decimal hours as hours and minutes, keep the whole hours and multiply the decimal part by $60$.
**12-hour time** uses am and pm, whereas **24-hour time** uses four digits from $00{:}00$ to $23{:}59$.
For pm times, add $12$ to the hour except at $12$ pm. Midnight is $00{:}00$ and noon is $12{:}00$.
steps: Choose the requested units. Multiply for a smaller unit or divide for a larger one, using 60 for seconds/minutes/hours and 24 for hours/days. For mixed units, convert each part and add; to split a total, keep whole units and convert the remainder.

For decimal hours and hours–minutes–seconds, use the calculator DMS key to enter or display the parts. Check with minutes divided by 60 and seconds divided by 3600, or multiply decimal remainders by 60. Round only the final value to the requested precision.

For clock formats, keep minutes unchanged. In 24-hour time, use 00 for 12 am and keep 12 pm; add 12 to other pm hours. To read 24-hour time, 00 means 12 am, 01–11 are am, 12 is pm and 13–23 subtract 12 and use pm.

workedExamples.question_text:
Convert to the requested smaller units.
(a) $3$ minutes $47$ seconds to seconds
(b) $2$ days $11$ hours to hours
(c) $1$ day $6$ hours $13$ minutes to minutes

Convert to whole larger units and the remaining smaller units.
(a) $428$ minutes to hours and minutes
(b) $83$ hours to days and hours
(c) $8429$ seconds to hours, minutes and seconds
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $428=7\times60+8$, so $7\text{ h }8\text{ min}$.
(b) $83=3\times24+11$, so $3\text{ days }11\text{ h}$.
(c) $8429=2\times3600+1229$.
$1229=20\times60+29$.
The interval is $2\text{ h }20\text{ min }29\text{ s}$.

workedExamples.question_text: Use a calculator to write $5.28472$ hours as hours, minutes and seconds. Give seconds to 2 decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Enter $5.28472$ and use the DMS key to display hours, minutes and seconds.
The display gives $5$ hours $17$ minutes $4.992$ seconds.
Check the parts: $0.28472\times60=17.0832$ minutes.
$0.0832\times60=4.992$ seconds.
Rounding only the seconds gives $5\text{ h }17\text{ min }4.99\text{ s}$.

workedExamples.question_text: Use a calculator to write $1$ hour $28$ minutes $43$ seconds as decimal hours, to 3 decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use the DMS key to enter the hours, minutes and seconds, then display the decimal value.
$1+\dfrac{28}{60}+\dfrac{43}{3600}=1.478611\ldots$ hours.
The interval is approximately $1.479\text{ h}$, to 3 decimal places.

workedExamples.question_text:
Convert the clock times.
(a) $9{:}26\text{ pm}$ to 24-hour time
(b) $12{:}38\text{ am}$ to 24-hour time
(c) $16{:}53$ to 12-hour time
(d) $12{:}07$ to 12-hour time
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Add $12$ to the pm hour: $9+12=21$, giving $21{:}26$.
(b) The hour after midnight is $00$, giving $00{:}38$.
(c) $16-12=4$, giving $4{:}53\text{ pm}$.
(d) Keep the noon hour as $12$, giving $12{:}07\text{ pm}$.

foundation.question_text: Convert $193\text{ minutes}$ to hours and minutes.
foundation.solution_text:
Convert minutes to hours and remainder minutes.
$193 \div 60 = 3\text{ with a remainder of } 13$
$= 3\text{ h } 13\text{ min}$

Convert minutes to seconds and add remaining seconds.
$47\text{ min} = 47 \times 60 = 2820\text{ s}$
$\text{Total seconds} = 2820 + 12$
$= 2832\text{ s}$

foundation.question_text: Convert $100\text{ hours}$ to days and hours.
foundation.solution_text:
Convert hours to days ($24\text{ hours/day}$) and leftover hours.
$100 \div 24 = 4\text{ with a remainder of } 4$
$= 4\text{ days } 4\text{ h}$

foundation.question_text: Convert $5\text{ days } 17\text{ hours}$ to total hours.
foundation.solution_text:
Convert days to hours and add the extra hours.
$5\text{ days} = 5 \times 24 = 120\text{ h}$
$\text{Total hours} = 120 + 17$
$= 137\text{ h}$

foundation.question_text: Convert $3.75\text{ hours}$ to hours and minutes.
foundation.solution_text:
Convert decimal hours to whole hours and minutes.
$\text{Whole hours} = 3\text{ h}$
$\text{Minutes} = 0.75 \times 60 = 45\text{ min}$
$= 3\text{ h } 45\text{ min}$

foundation.question_text: Convert $2.4\text{ hours}$ to hours and minutes.
foundation.solution_text:
Convert decimal fraction $0.4\text{ h}$ to minutes.
$\text{Minutes} = 0.4 \times 60 = 24\text{ min}$
$= 2\text{ h } 24\text{ min}$

foundation.question_text: Convert $2\text{ hours } 37\text{ minutes}$ to decimal hours, rounded to 3 decimal places.
foundation.solution_text:
Convert sexagesimal minutes to decimal hours.
$\text{Decimal hours} = 2 + \dfrac{37}{60}$
$= 2 + 0.616666...$
$\approx 2.617\text{ hours}$

development.question_text: Convert $10\,000\text{ seconds}$ to hours, minutes, and seconds.
development.solution_text:
Convert seconds to hours ($3600\text{ s/h}$), minutes, and seconds.
$10\,000 \div 3600 = 2\text{ hours remainder } 2800\text{ s}$
$2800 \div 60 = 46\text{ minutes remainder } 40\text{ s}$
$= 2\text{ h } 46\text{ min } 40\text{ s}$

development.question_text: Convert $3\text{ days } 9\text{ hours } 45\text{ minutes}$ into total minutes.
development.solution_text:
Convert days and hours to minutes, then sum.
$3\text{ days} = 3 \times 24 \times 60 = 4320\text{ min}$
$9\text{ hours} = 9 \times 60 = 540\text{ min}$
$\text{Total minutes} = 4320 + 540 + 45$
$= 4905\text{ min}$

development.question_text: Convert $3.27145\text{ hours}$ to hours, minutes, and seconds (seconds to 2 decimal places).
development.solution_text:
Successively multiply decimal remainders by $60$.
$\text{Whole hours} = 3\text{ h}$
$0.27145 \times 60 = 16.287\text{ min} \implies 16\text{ min}$
$0.287 \times 60 = 17.22\text{ s}$
$= 3\text{ h } 16\text{ min } 17.22\text{ s}$

development.question_text: Convert $1\text{ hour } 33\text{ minutes } 27\text{ seconds}$ to decimal hours, correct to 4 decimal places.
development.solution_text:
Express minutes over $60$ and seconds over $3600$.
$\text{Decimal hours} = 1 + \dfrac{33}{60} + \dfrac{27}{3600}$
$= 1 + 0.55 + 0.0075$
$= 1.5575\text{ hours}$

development.question_text: Convert $4\text{ hours } 15\text{ minutes}$ to decimal hours.
development.solution_text:
Convert minutes to decimal hours.
$\text{Decimal hours} = 4 + \dfrac{15}{60}$
$= 4 + 0.25$
$= 4.25\text{ hours}$

development.question_text: Convert $10{:}30\text{ pm}$ and $2{:}00\text{ am}$ to 24-hour time.
Convert $12{:}15\text{ am}$ and $12{:}45\text{ pm}$ to 24-hour time.
development.solution_text:
$12{:}15\text{ am}$ is in the first hour of the day $\to 00{:}15$
$12{:}45\text{ pm}$ is in the afternoon noon hour $\to 12{:}45$
Answers are $00{:}15$ and $12{:}45$.

mastery.question_text: Convert $15.282\text{ hours}$ to hours, minutes, and seconds (rounded to 1 decimal place of seconds).
mastery.solution_text:
Convert decimal hour remainder to sexagesimal components.
$\text{Whole hours} = 15\text{ h}$
$0.282 \times 60 = 16.92\text{ min} \implies 16\text{ min}$
$0.92 \times 60 = 55.2\text{ s}$
$= 15\text{ h } 16\text{ min } 55.2\text{ s}$

mastery.question_text:
A flight departure board displays four departure times: $08{:}15$, $13{:}05$, $21{:}45$, and $00{:}35$.
Convert each time to 12-hour format with am/pm.
Convert the following 24-hour clock times to 12-hour time: $17{:}56$, $03{:}18$, and $23{:}00$.
mastery.solution_text:
Subtract $12$ from hours $\ge 13$ and attach pm; keep hours $< 12$ and attach am.
$17{:}56 = 17{:}56 - 12{:}00 = 5{:}56\text{ pm}$
$03{:}18 = 3{:}18\text{ am}$
$23{:}00 = 23{:}00 - 12{:}00 = 11{:}00\text{ pm}$
Times are $5{:}56\text{ pm}$, $3{:}18\text{ am}$, and $11{:}00\text{ pm}$.
